{{Quote|Hod Ha'ran, the trickster, agent of fickle fortune...|[[Tor Vizsla]]|<ref name="TBHC" />}}
'''Hod Ha'ran''' was a [[God/Legends|deity]] in the ancient [[Mandalorian religion]]. Known as a trickster god by the early [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] people, Hod Ha'ran was viewed as an agent of the fickle nature of fortune.<ref name="TBHC" />

Over [[Time/Legends|time]], worship<ref name="TMPaC">{{InsiderCite|86|The Mandalorians: People and Culture}}</ref> of Hod Ha'ran<ref name="TBHC" /> and the other Mandalorian gods, like [[Kad Ha'rangir]] the Destroyer and [[Arasuum]] the sloth-god, fell into decline.<ref name="TMPaC" /> The Mandalorians turned to the singular worship of war itself for a time,<ref name="HotM">{{InsiderCite|80|The History of the Mandalorians: Exploring the Evolution of a Mighty Race of Warriors}}</ref> before turning their backs on those beliefs as well as the [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]] passed.<ref name="TMPaC" /> However, Hod Ha'ran and the Mandalorian gods were not completely forgotten: millennia later, [[Death Watch/Legends|Death Watch]] founder [[Tor Vizsla]] spoke of Hod Ha'ran and the ancient gods in a manifesto he prepared,<ref name="TBHC" /> and by [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], the Mandalorian [[Soldier/Legends|soldier]] [[Kal Skirata]] knew of their former place in Mandalorian mythology.<ref name="O66">''[[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Hod Ha'ran was first introduced to ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]], now part of the [[Star Wars Legends|Legends]] continuity, in the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] reference book ''[[The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett]]''. [[Author/Legends|Co-authored]] by [[Daniel Wallace]], [[Jason Fry]], and [[Ryder Windham]], the book was released on [[October 15]], [[2013]].
